episode.subject: pale pitcher plant
episode.title: One more tremor
episode.body:
The bee clung to my flower and pushed her head beneath a petal.

The stem dipped. When she let go, it sprang back.

I mistook the trembling for her feet and waited through another little shiver.

proposals.admission: Lead passed exact image, literal prose, continuity and primary CC0 record; integrated after existing flower episode.
proposals.visualReview: Exact published frame opened individually. A clearly visible dark bee with pale thorax patch clings at the left edge of the second yellow-green pendant flower. Its feet grip the petal edge and head approaches the petal fold; curved stalk visible above. Several other flowers and upright pitchers supply clear whole-plant context. No insect silhouette guessing.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Contact is visible; head passing farther under petal, stem dipping, elastic return and bee leaving are plausible fictional sequence, not documented motion. The photograph does not demonstrate special neural sensation or leg-count perception. Female pronoun is fictional characterization, not insect-sex identification. No bee species, pollination, pollen removal, meal or intentional trap closure claimed.
proposals.continuity: Established Sarracenia alata, rooted Big Thicket wet-pine-savanna home30.6/-94.4 and separate passive pitchers/pendant flowers retained. This occurs after admitted flower-butterfly episode without referring to a tracked insect or same photographed specimen. No new avatar/identity.
proposals.proseReview: A visitor leaves but the flower continues to move; Hester prolongs the presence through that physical aftereffect. Unlike the butterfly episode, no expected capture or approval of release supplies the turn. Her quiet possessiveness continues. Risk: this may still repeat flower-contact affection too closely; root must judge, and the prior source-only hold is not erased.
